title: Grandmaster Naroditsky | Chess Speedrun | 1310
openingName: Playing a piece down (a discipline lesson)

moves.spoken: A deliberate handicap experiment — Black jettisons the dark-squared bishop on a3. The point isn't the sacrifice; it's what you do once you're a piece down.

The first and most important lesson when you're down material: do NOT spiral. Players blunder a piece and then, out of a false sense of necessity, throw away rook after rook pretending it was all planned. Instead, keep your remaining pieces, play sound chess, and make your opponent earn the win.
teaches: don’t compound a blunder — play on soundly

moves.spoken: And a real resource even here — we can tempt White to trade on f6 and recapture with a pawn. The doubled pawns look ugly but are a blessing in disguise: they hand us dark-square control and open lines toward White's slightly loose setup.
teaches: recapture toward the center for dark-square control
